definitions.explanation: The native Japanese word for ten, the final element in the {一|ひと}つ, {二|ふた}つ, {三|みっ}つ ... {十|とお} counting sequence. This series stops at ten; from eleven onward, Japanese uses the Sino-Japanese system ({十一|じゅういち}).

examples.japanese: りんごを{十|とお}{数|かぞ}える。
{息子|むすこ}は{十|とお}になった。
{一|ひと}つ、{二|ふた}つと{数|かぞ}えていって、{十|とお}でちょうど{箱|はこ}がいっぱいになった。
examples.english: Counting one, two, and so on, the box was exactly full at ten.

notes:
Last word in the native counting sequence: {一|ひと}つ, {二|ふた}つ, {三|みっ}つ, {四|よっ}つ, {五|いつ}つ, {六|むっ}つ, {七|なな}つ, {八|やっ}つ, {九|ここの}つ, {十|とお}. Notice that {十|とお} alone takes no つ suffix.

USAGE:
- For general items, especially with no special counter: ringo o {十|とお}
- For age: {十|とお}になる ("turn ten") is a slightly literary alternative to {十歳|じゅっさい}
- After ten, switch to the Sino-Japanese system: {十一|じゅういち}, {十二|じゅうに}, etc.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {十|じゅう}: ten (Sino-Japanese) — used with most counters ({十冊|じゅっさつ}, {十人|じゅうにん})
- {十歳|じゅっさい}: ten years old — standard expression for age
